howTheseWereProduced: Minted for the PRUVZ-97 release by conformance/mint-conformance.mjs (committed for provenance; re-running produces different signed bytes because ECDSA and the nonces are randomized — the published bytes are the agreement point and conformance/v1/ is immutable). An ephemeral four-version trust registry (publish, rotate in, retire, back-dated revoke), seals over the published examples/valid/verified-refund.packet.json, an RFC 6962 log with genuinely signed forked, rolled-back and insert-forged checkpoints modeling a compromised deployment, and a synthetic RFC 3161 authority whose root is published here for pinning. Expected reports were produced by lib/verify.mjs at mint time and reviewed case by case against the layer specifications before publication. Every conformant runtime must reproduce every verdict, reason-code set, dimension status and returned state independently, without reading the expectations.

cases.description: The complete coherent bundle with pinned TSA roots — the only reachable FULLY_VERIFIED.
The same bundle without pinned TSA roots: bindings check, authority honestly NOT_EVALUATED.
PRE_CUSTOMER_DEFAULT material with no anchors: the cost-gated absence is reported, and FULLY_VERIFIED is unreachable.
Replaying the accepted bundle against its own returned state changes nothing.
The baseline re-serialized with reversed member order and whitespace is the same logical bundle and yields the identical report.
A bundle file with a duplicated member name is two documents in one byte string; every runtime refuses it as unusable input.
A truncated export is not a weaker bundle; it is unusable input.
One summary edited after sealing: the record no longer hashes to the digest its seal names.
The same instant respelled with a zero fraction commits identically — normalization is not tampering, and the report equals the baseline.
A different instant is a different committed value.
Two valid seals swapped between records: each signature is genuine and attests to the other subject.
Seals genuinely made for another tenant, presented under the caller-pinned tenant.
Seals genuinely made for another action over identical content.
A complete, internally consistent registry under a different root: everything verifies under ITS root and nothing verifies under the pin.
A valid ES256 seal by a key the registry never published.
The trust root sealing evidence: the two powers that must never meet.
Seals made while their key was ACTIVE stay valid after the key is retired; the retirement is noted, never punished.
Seals made before the declared, back-dated compromise: weakened (the boundary compares against self-asserted time), never full.
A seal whose committedAt falls at or after the declared compromise is a refusal.
A correctly signed OLDER registry presented to a verifier that already accepted a newer one — how a revocation is hidden.
A second, genuinely signed manifest at an already-held version: one version has one history.
A record scrubbed from packet, seals and proofs: the remaining proofs no longer lead to the honest checkpointed head.
Two leaves swapped and proofs recomputed: order is data, and the honest head refuses the reordered tree.
An insider inserts a leaf inside checkpointed history and signs the new head: no consistency proof can connect the honest head to it.
One flipped byte in an inclusion path.
One flipped byte in a consistency proof.
Two genuinely signed checkpoints numbered 2 with different heads served in one bundle.
The forked head presented to a verifier that already accepted the honest one.
A later, genuinely signed checkpoint covering fewer leaves: append-only means the tree never shrinks.
An old export presented after newer history was held: reported as unconnected history, and the held state never regresses.
A genuine receipt for the registry presented as the checkpoint anchor: the token binds to something else.
A replayed token: the record names a request nonce the token does not carry.
The genuine token verified against a different pinned authority root: trust is the caller pin, never the embedded chain.
The token binds (its imprint is untouched) but its signature bytes were altered: half two refuses what half one alone cannot.
A pending anchor is not a witness, and is never reported as one.
An anchor whose subject carries a tenant identifier violates the privacy boundary by construction and is refused as malformed.
Material genuinely claiming CUSTOMER_PRODUCTION with no anchors: the claim the packet cannot prove never reaches FULLY_VERIFIED.
A transported checkpoint whose profile was upgraded after signing: the signed bytes changed.
Seals and checkpoints genuinely produced under different profiles: reported, never averaged.
The packet timeline shortened while the served seal set still names the removed record.
Proof material without the payload: proves the sealed record existed and is covered — and is never presented as payload verification.
